title: Integer linear threshold representation
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f$ be a function from the Boolean cube $\\{-1,1\\}^n$ to $\\{\\pm1\\}$. If $f$ is represented as the sign of a real affine linear form, then there are integer coefficients $a_0,a_1,\\ldots,a_n$ such that, for every $x\\in\\{-1,1\\}^n$, $f(x)$ is the sign of $a_0+\\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i$, and this integer-coefficient affine form is nonzero at every point of the cube.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ has a real linear threshold representation
